turns.prompt:
You are given one attached CSV file:
  - nlo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose properties are
    NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar` (the crystal
    structure, in POSCAR format).

No property values are provided. Using your knowledge of crystal optics,
crystal symmetry and structure-property relationships, predict which
candidates have the HIGHEST birefringence at 1064 nm, then select the 5 best
candidates from the pool.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
The magnitude of birefringence is governed by the anisotropy of the electronic polarizability density. Cubic crystals therefore have \(\Delta n=0\). The largest values arise when intrinsically anisotropic structural units (planar \(\pi\)-conjugated groups or stereo-active lone-pair cations) are co-aligned in a low-dimensional packing.

Direct inspection of the POSCAR lattices and atomic coordinates identifies three NaSrBS\(_3\) polymorphs (c040, c042, c043) in which every boron is trigonal-planar, the three B–S bonds lie in a common plane, and all \(\mathrm{BS}_3\) triangles are strictly parallel. The stacking axis is the short \(\approx4.2\,\text{Å}\) cell edge, producing a quasi-2-D arrangement of highly anisotropic anionic groups. This motif is the direct analogue of the carbonate layers in calcite, but with the far more polarizable sulfide ligands, and is therefore expected to yield the highest \(\Delta n\) at 1064 nm.

The next-strongest anisotropy occurs in the 1-D iodide c039 (\(\mathrm{RbGeI}_3\)). The cell metric (\(4.56\times10.63\times17.11\,\text{Å}\)) together with the presence of stereo-active \(\mathrm{Ge}^{2+}\) lone pairs indicates isolated \(\mathrm{GeI}_3\) chains; both the chain topology and the lone-pair alignment generate a very large polarizability contrast.

A fifth, still strongly anisotropic candidate is the hexagonal chain compound c038 (\(\mathrm{Tl}_3\mathrm{SbS}_3\)), which combines two lone-pair cations (\(\mathrm{Tl}^+\), \(\mathrm{Sb}^{3+}\)) in a uniaxial packing.

All other entries are either cubic, three-dimensional tetrahedral networks (SiC polytypes, chalcopyrites, wurtzites), or contain only weakly anisotropic units, and therefore rank lower.

Final: c043, c040, c042, c039, c038
